text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The government presented a budget amendment to its controversial Eurotax proposal, raising the tax threshold for the self-employed to 15.2 million lire from 10 million. But in the ruling coalition foreign minister and leader of Italian Renewal party Lamberto Dini says changes are not enough and pensions should be cut (all).

* Commenting on judicial problems for Prime Minister Romano Prodi, National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini says "We are just asking for clarity." On Monday a magistrate asked for Prodi to be tried for alleged abuse of office during his chairmanship of state industrial holding IRI. The judge is expected to make a decision in January 1997 (all).

* A colleague of former magistrate Antonio Di Pietro says he knew Di Pietro would resign as early as April 1994. Di Pietro resigned on December 1994, amid fierce speculations of an alleged plot against him (all).

* Prodi asked a special body monitoring pensions to carry out a study on the impact of potential changes to current regulations. Trade unions say they are ready to stage a national strike if the government wants to bring forward reforming pensions to 1997 instead of 1998, as initially scheduled (all).

* Giovanni Agnelli, honorary chairman of Fiat, said a slight delay to Italy's entry into European economic and monetary union would not be a "tragedy". Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti said Italy should "renegotiate with its European partners the terms of its participation to EMU". Previously Romiti had been quoted as saying Italy should delay its entry by three years (all).

* Roberto Colaninno, chief executive of troubled information technology group Olivetti warned the Italian parliament against opening an inquiry into the company's affairs, saying the prospect of such a probe could finish the group off (all).

* The Treasury dropped its attempt to raise its voting rights on privatised companies, which would have given it 34 pct voting rights in insurance company Ina. The previous threshold of 5 pct voting rights was reinstated (Corriere della Sera, Repubblica).
-- Today financial daily Sole 24 Ore was not available.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
